_schema: steps[] runs as a sequence of stages. Each entry is either:
_schema_object: - an object: a single step that runs alone, waits for previous stage to finish
_schema_array: - an array of step objects: those steps run in PARALLEL within the same stage
_schema_kinds: Three step kinds (each a JSON object with a `name` field):
_schema_download: download_install: HTTP-download `url`, then run with `args` (silent flags).
_schema_script: run_script:       write `script` verbatim to a temp .cmd and execute via cmd /c.
_schema_script_ref: or use `script_ref` (resolved at parse time to a script
_schema_script_ref3: batch bodies out of this JSON file).
_schema_extract: download_extract: HTTP-download `url`, extract via tar.exe to `extract_to`
_schema_extract2: (or a temp dir if empty), then optionally run `script` with
_schema_drivers: There is no driver step and no driver media. The system disk is NVMe and the NIC an e1000e, devices Windows drives with in-box drivers from the first boot of Setup on, so nothing is injected into WinPE or the offline image and there is no guest-tools bundle to run. The one driver Windows lacks is accel-virt's, which the payload ISO carries (see _schema_gpu).
_schema_gpu: There is deliberately NO DXVK / VKD3D-Proton step here. Those guest-side copies existed for the old render server, which offered no Direct3D of its own: DXVK and VKD3D-Proton translated it, inside the guest, onto that server's Vulkan driver. accel-virt's driver package carries a native D3D11/12 user-mode driver (avumd.dll) beside its Vulkan, OpenGL and OpenCL ones, and is signed in specialize (LswAvSign.ps1) and installed at SetupComplete (LswPromote.ps1) from C:\av, staged from the payload ISO, not by a setup step: it wants SYSTEM, and the steady-state VM's only display is that device.
_schema_promote: Admin promotion is NOT a setup step: it runs from C:\Windows\Setup\Scripts\SetupComplete.cmd → LswPromote.ps1 (SYSTEM, before first AutoLogon) so the account is admin when LSA builds its logon token — no re-logon needed. The autounattend <Group>Administrators> is live-proven not to stick on Win11 26200 and `net localgroup /add` fails 1317 there; PowerShell Add-LocalGroupMember works.
